This asymmetry in the structure of the nucleotides gives the DNA strands their directionality, with one strand running in the 5' to 3' direction and the complementary strand running in the opposite direction, or 3' to 5'. Q: Why is the Gospel of John said at the end of Catholic Mass?
A: "The Gospel of John, specifically the Prologue (John 1:1\u201314), is said at the end of the Catholic Mass as the \"Last Gospel.\" This practice originated as a private devotional practice by the priest and was gradually incorporated into the rubrics of the Mass. As the load (resistance) decreases or the demand for power increases, the current drawn will rise accordingly

single_squad_dev_1996
What distinguishes peremptory norms from other principles of customary law?
A: ["Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Customary international law", "Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Customary international law", "Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Custom (law)", "International law", "Sources of international law"]
Q: What distinguishes peremptory norms from other principles of customary law?
A: "Peremptory norms, also known as jus cogens, are distinguished from other principles of customary law by their fundamental nature and the fact that they cannot be violated or derogated from by any state through international treaties or local customs. While ordinary customary law allows for alteration of obligations between states, peremptory norms are universally accepted as overriding all other sources of international law. Examples of peremptory norms include the prohibitions against genocide, torture, slavery, and aggressive war. These norms are considered so essential to the international community that any treaty conflicting with them is deemed void under Article 53 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties."
A: Peremptory norms, also known as jus cogens, are distinguished from other principles of customary law by their fundamental nature and the fact that they cannot be violated or derogated from by any state through international treaties or local customs. While ordinary customary law allows for alteration of obligations between states, peremptory norms are universally accepted as overriding all other sources of international law. Examples of peremptory norms include the prohibitions against genocide, torture, slavery, and aggressive war. These norms are considered so essential to the international community that any treaty conflicting with them is deemed void under Article 53 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties
